restrictions: Two distinct 64-byte messages (pairs of canonical Pallas field elements) with equal digests for the Orchard hash with 23 partial rounds (poseidon-orchard-r23-prefix-v1, digest = state[0], whole element compared). The messages are the line inverse message(W) of proof.md Section 2; both are canonical by construction.

Cost model orchard-field-ram-v2, C = 216 + 21*23 = 699. Prices used: canonical field ADD, SUB and MUL 1/C each; every 256-bit word primitive 1/C; exponentiation and inversion charged as their counted constituent operations; a target compression is one unit. No permutation call is charged as a unit.

Ledger (proof.md Section 7): a walk step is 419.75 charged operations (416 field: 249 MUL + 167 ADD, plus 3.75 word; the sparse equivalent form, listing in proof.md Section 3, with the partial rounds' linear layers absorbed offline into the running bases); the filed search is one trail of S0 = 169428545758018874978475100145551477411 steps (the tight trail n0 = 169346087099996799090729207472420809487 plus the detection window 82458658022075887745892673130667924); recovery at most 3*(gmax+16) evaluations at 419.75 + 6 each plus at most four scans at 109,668 word operations each; dp-table work at most 27,414 events at at most 137,081 word operations each (5 word operations per probe over the packed 27,413-entry table + 16); PRG 2 coin draws at 264; setup 2000; fifth roots 2286; offline derivation bounded by 2^41 word operations, charged inside time_log2. Total 71342505199651044874437946853804379242904.75 operations / C = 699 = 1.0206e38 target compressions; log2 = 126.262737, filed 126.26274 (rounded up).

Memory: 27,413 dp-table entries of one 32-byte word (high 126 bits of the value OR its index) plus a 16-bit side field each, one 32-byte start word, at most 103,644 bytes of code, 5,600 constants and 7,200 register bytes: 1,048,518 bytes total, under 2^20, so the normalized memory term of the score is 0 (proof.md Section 8). The threshold is below 2^16, so the stored key is injective on dp values and reconstruction is exact.

Success probability at least 0.39 at the filed tight trail budget n0 = 169346087099996799090729207472420809487, at which the uniform-random-function lemma of proof.md Section 5 (c = 1) gives exactly 0.390000000 in 80-digit Decimal. The real-map transfer is the bare premise H1 (claim.json H1-random-walk-rate, proof.md Section 6): an assumption, no proof is known, NO hazard margin is filed. The measured hazard multiplier (pooled 1.0044, 95% profile-likelihood CI [0.9891, 1.0198], no slope across widths; every measured cell lower bound at least 0.9080) is consistent with the premise; at the pooled lower endpoint the success at n0 is 0.3867, just under the minimum, so the claim is evidence-consistent but not evidence-forced. This is the tight-n0 filing convention of the accepted r=22 and r=24+ incumbents.

The step program, the single-trail search with its recovery, the budget solve, the measurement and analysis sources are printed in full in proof.md Appendices A-C (standard library only); the organizer experiment is experiments/exp_lowbits.py with experiments/manifest.json (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask on the first 14 bits, 256 trials; local run 256/256 verified pairs, byte-identical on repeat).

heuristics.statement: The filed trail has n0 = 169346087099996799090729207472420809487 steps, the tight random-function trail budget at which the uniform-random-function lemma (proof.md Section 5, c = 1) bounds success at exactly 0.39. Premise: for the attempt's coins (rho0 and x0, uniform 254-bit words), the distinguished-point single-trail search of proof.md Section 4 on the real map F(x) = digest(message(x + rho0)) / OUTSCALE, at the trail budget n0, succeeds with probability at least 0.39. H1 is our theory that, for this search, the fixed map with a random rho0 behaves like a uniformly random function; this is an assumption and no proof is known. No hazard tolerance margin is filed (the tight convention of the accepted r=22/r=24+ incumbents). Same-map cross-evidence: the incumbent entry ab786fc (a dependency) publishes measurements of exactly this walk-map family (output divided by OUTSCALE_r) at r = 7, 23 and 56, on the bit-identical r = 23 map; the participant campaign of proof.md Section 6 measured the same construction with the output rescaled by the fixed nonzero constant LAMBDA_lean * OUTSCALE (disclosed).
heuristics.scope: Target poseidon-orchard-r23-prefix-v1, inputs on the line of proof.md Section 2, one search with the parameters of proof.md Section 4 (walk budget S1 = 178597435891429200878561991096629710601 evaluations). Not claimed for other round counts or budgets. Only the success probability rests on this premise; the step program, the search and recovery, the ledger and the memory are proved or checked exactly (proof.md Sections 3, 4, 7, 8).
heuristics.extrapolation: Organizer-run experiment lowbits-birthday (python-message-pairs-v1, digest-xor-mask, 256 trials; proof.md Section 10): reduced-width witness on this target's own digest at r=23, first 14 bits, fresh random inputs, at most 1200 evaluations per trial; local run of the same event returned 256/256 verified pairs, byte-identical on repeat; it witnesses no gross low-bit structure and infers no probability. Participant measurements (proof.md Section 6, Appendix C): first-repeat walks on the real r=23 map truncated to w in [16, 20, 24, 28, 32, 36] bits, fresh (rho0, start) per walk, every walk to its exact first repeat, 16380 walks, exact discrete first-repeat likelihood with bounded series tail; pooled hazard multiplier 1.0044, 95% profile-likelihood CI [0.9891, 1.0198], no slope across widths - consistent with the tight premise (multiplier 1) but not dominating it: at the pooled lower endpoint 0.9891 the success at n0 is 0.3867, just under the 0.39 minimum. The extrapolation from widths 16-36 to width 254 is the premise itself; the measurements do not bound the full-width multiplier.
heuristics.limitations: The organizer experiment is one width (14 bits), one round count, a witness-only event on the digest, not on the walk map, and cannot validate this premise. The participant measurements reach outputs of at most 36 bits and first-repeat indexes of order 2^19 steps; they show the random-function first-repeat law on the real round function at these widths and do not bound the rate at 254 bits. The interval is a profile-likelihood interval, asymptotic in the number of walks and conditional on the hazard-multiplier family; it is evidence about the multiplier, not a bound. On a single fixed map the success over starts varies with that map's cycle structure; the attempt draws rho0 as a coin and the premise concerns the average over rho0.
